variance.likelihood_comparison: only variance candidates conditional on the same fixed mean; not ARMA likelihood
variance.bic_parameter_count: variance parameters only; shared fixed mean not counted
variance.evaluation_target: same squared fixed-ARMA forecast innovation; noisy proxy, not observed variance
variance.boundary_policy: continue observation index across sessions without overnight returns
variance.diagnostic_reference: ordinary asymptotic ARCH-LM and Ljung-Box; approximate after sequential fitting
notes: Fitting, scaling, lag choices and BIC selection do not use test observations.
OOS recursion uses the previous actual innovation, never the current/future one.

No Diebold-Mariano test between these candidates: constant subset ARCH(1) subset GARCH(1,1) are all nested in each other (each is the next with one more coefficient set to zero), and Aula 4 explicitly teaches DM is not appropriate for nested models.
A better variance forecast is not a better point forecast of returns.
A rejected standardized-residual Ljung-Box still indicates limitations of the mean equation.
